Washington Commanders @ San Francisco 49ers

Jacory Croskey-Merritt lands on injured reserve: Washington's leading rusher will miss at least four games with a groin injury.

Washington has relied on Croskey-Merritt as its early-down back and Rachaad White as its receiving back this season, with Austin Ekeler returning to the mix when White missed time. Ekeler entered this game less than 100% healthy after being limited in practice all week with a chest injury. The Commanders also activated Jeremy McNichols from injured reserve earlier in the day, eliminating the need to elevate Craig Reynolds from the practice squad, as they had earlier in the season. That left Washington with an interesting combination of three running backs who have each served as the team's third-down back at different points over the past three seasons.

White handled the bulk of the work tonight, with Ekeler occasionally rotating in and McNichols not seeing his first offensive snaps until the third quarter. While White dominated snaps, it's worth noting that Washington lost the time-of-possession battle, giving White several extended breaks without necessarily needing another back to spell him. Ekeler's lingering chest injury may have also contributed to the lopsided workload.

White can generally be considered a fantasy starter for the next three games based on his dominant share of the backfield snaps, although there's no guarantee the Commanders will maintain this rotation going forward.

Commanders adjust without Terry McLaurin: The Commanders briefly had their wide receiver room intact before another injury forced them to adjust.

Washington was without McLaurin (hamstring) in Week 4 and Stefon Diggs (hamstring) in Week 5. Both players, along with Treylon Burks (shoulder), were limited in practice at times this past week. While Jaylin Lane remains out for the season, this was the healthiest Washington's wide receiver room had looked in several weeks.

Washington opened with McLaurin as its lead receiver, Burks joining him in 12 personnel and Diggs and Antonio Williams joining him in 11 personnel. That alignment lasted just two drives before McLaurin left with a knee injury. He was carted to the locker room with an air cast on his leg and quickly ruled out, suggesting the injury could be serious.

Washington shifted to a heavy rotation of players in 12 and 13 personnel, while Burks, Williams and Diggs were the primary receivers in 11 personnel. Dyami Brown rotated in at times, while Luke McCaffrey saw his first offensive snaps of the season.

Burks was injured in the final two minutes while attempting to catch the game-winning touchdown. He wasn't available for Washington's final two-minute drive, when Brown, Williams and Diggs served as the three receivers. Burks would be a solid waiver-wire target going forward, but only if McLaurin's injury is as serious as it appeared and Burks' own injury isn't serious.

Chig Okonkwo has excellent route participation rates: Okonkwo was almost always running a route whenever the Commanders called a pass play.

Okonkwo was a popular sleeper tight end this offseason after the Commanders acquired him from the Tennessee Titans. He was off to a strong start in Week 1 in terms of playing time before suffering a hamstring injury that kept him out in Weeks 2 and 3. He was then eased back into action in Week 4.

Last week, his playing time increased to 71% of the snaps. He was almost always the tight end on the field in 11 personnel and played 91% of the snaps in 13 personnel, but was rarely on the field in 12 personnel. This week, he rotated out at times in 13 personnel, which wasn't a concern because those were mostly run plays. He also remained on the field for most plays out of 12 personnel. As a result, he ranked among the league leaders in route participation at tight end this week, joining Brock Bowers, Isaiah Likely, Trey McBride and George Kittle.

Okonkwo caught seven passes for 69 yards, leading the team in receiving yards. The Commanders have their bye week next week, but Okonkwo would be a strong option for anyone looking for a tight end who could potentially start for their fantasy team later in the season.

The 49ers adjust without all of their top receivers: Deebo Samuel Sr. was inactive for this game, while Mike Evans left before halftime.

San Francisco has used nine wide receivers this season. De’Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson have landed on injured reserve, while KhaDarel Hodge was released with an injury. Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk started the season on injured reserve, and Samuel didn't practice all week because of a hamstring injury before being ruled out Saturday.

This left Evans, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks as the available receivers on the 53-man roster, with Malik Turner elevated from the practice squad. Evans didn't practice all week because of rib and Achilles injuries and was questionable, but he was active.

San Francisco used a straightforward wide receiver rotation, with Evans as the X receiver, Watkins at Z and Cowing joining them in 11 personnel, often in the slot. Cooks backed up Evans, while Turner backed up Watkins. The 49ers typically kept their X receiver on the field in 22 personnel. Evans played 25 of the first 38 snaps before heading to the locker room just before halftime because his Achilles injury was bothering him. He was ruled out shortly after halftime, but not before catching three passes for 94 yards.

Cooks took over as the X receiver following Evans' departure. San Francisco faces the Atlanta Falcons next week, a favorable matchup for wide receivers, before heading into its bye week. If the 49ers decide to sit Evans next week to give him additional time to recover, Cooks would be the best waiver-wire pickup from this group, as he's in the strongest position to produce.

Miscellaneous Notes

With the injuries at wide receiver, San Francisco ran five plays with both Kaelon Black and Christian McCaffrey on the field, with McCaffrey lined up as a wide receiver. The 49ers hadn't used this personnel grouping at any point over the first five weeks.

San Francisco running back Kyle Juszczyk was back in the lineup after missing last week's game with a knee injury. He was limited in practice Thursday before being upgraded to a full participant Friday.

49ers wide receiver Christian Kirk returned to practice from injured reserve Thursday. He was limited in practice with a calf injury and was listed as questionable, but he remains on injured reserve.

Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota didn't practice all week because of a knee injury and was ruled out Saturday, marking his second straight absence.

The Vikings wrapped up their Week 5 matchup against the Saints with a win, but they were also down multiple starters with various injuries. However, last week's conveniently placed bye allowed many of them to get healthy ahead of a Week 7 date with the Colts.

Despite the win, the Vikings were without Jordan Addison, Christian Darrisaw and more against New Orleans. So, who could be back, and who might be out for some time yet?

Here is the latest on the Vikings' injuries coming out of the bye.

Vikings who could return in Week 7

Jordan Mason, RB

Mason was put on short-term IR after injuring his thumb in Week 1. Aaron Jones was left as a one-man wrecking crew and was an absolute workhorse in Mason's absence, notching 97 touches during the four-week recovery. But with Mason now on the mend, it looks like Jones may get a bit of a rest in Week 7.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert reported on Monday that the Vikings have activated Mason from IR and expect him back at Wednesday's practice ahead of their matchup against Indianapolis, although his potential workload is still unclear.

Jordan Addison, WR

Addison was close to suiting up against the Saints in Week 5, according to head coach Kevin O'Connell, so he should be a sure thing to play against the Colts this weekend after two weeks of recovery time. Addison had been nursing a hamstring injury and tested it pregame against New Orleans but couldn't get to 100%. He'll be very close to that number now.

Addison has just 11 catches this year and needs some big games moving forward to earn a huge extension this offseason.

T.J. Hockenson, TE

The Vikings lost Hockenson on the second play of their opening drive against New Orleans, and the tight end was placed into the concussion protocol after the game. Every injury is different, but he'll likely clear in time to suit up Sunday.

If he can't go, Minnesota will get another strong dose of Bartholomew, who racked up five catches in Hockenson's absence in Week 5.

Christian Darrisaw, LT

Darrisaw left the Miami game with a concussion and was put into the protocol. He had initially left the game with a neck injury before returning briefly, then left the contest for good after experiencing concussion symptoms. Darrisaw has had a bit more time to recover than Hockenson, so his status should be good for Week 7, but both will need to be fully cleared before taking the field.

This most recent missed game now assures that Darrisaw will go six straight seasons with at least one spent on the sidelines. As talented as he is, Darrisaw has never made it through a full 17-game season in his career.

Vikings who are out for the season

Both guard Donovan Jackson and tight end Josh Oliver are confirmed to be out for the year, with Jackson suffering a torn meniscus and Oliver a torn triceps. Joe Huber has filled in for Jackson, while the young duo of Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek have picked up the slack at tight end.

The Vikings also lost safety Jamal Adams before the season with a torn quadriceps, as well as edge rusher Tyler Batty with a torn ACL.

text:
Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores and the San Francisco 49ers held on to beat the Washington Commanders 23-17 on Monday night for their sixth straight win to open the season.

The Niners followed up an emotional win last week at division rival Seattle by building a 20-point lead and holding off the Commanders (1-4-1) with two late defensive stops.

“[The defense] did it for us all game, I’m proud of those guys ... our defense balled,” Purdy said after the game.

Jayden Daniels threw two touchdown passes in the second half to cut that 20-point deficit to 23-17, but Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass to Treylon Burks near the goalline with 1:54 to play to preserve the lead.

Washington got the ball back at its 46 with 52 seconds remaining and moved down to the 28 before Daniels was called for intentional grounding, giving the Commanders one last play from the 40. Daniels was then sacked by Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo before he could throw up a desperation pass.

The Niners extended their best start of a season since winning their first eight games in 2019 on the way to a Super Bowl appearance.

Purdy started the game fast with a 24-yard strike to Mike Evans, who later left the game with an achilles injury, on the third play of the game and an 11-yard touchdown to George Kittle to finish that drive. Purdy went 21 for 29 for 264 yards and officially became the highest-rated quarterback in NFL history as he passed the 1,500-attempt threshold to qualify. His 105.6 rating is ahead of Lamar Jackson’s 102.7.

The Commanders were unable to bounce back from last week’s tie against the New York Giants, when they mismanaged the clock in overtime to cost them a chance at a game-winning field goal.

The game was one-sided early with the 49ers scoring touchdowns on the first two drives on Purdy’s pass to Kittle and a one-yard run by McCaffrey.

San Francisco expanded the lead to 20-3 late in the half on McCaffrey’s second touchdown run as the Niners gained as many first downs (17) in the first half as the Commanders ran plays.

The Commanders lost star receiver Terry McLaurin to what looked like a severe knee injury during the game, and he is likely to miss a significant amount of time.

“He’s a brother to me. It sucks,” Daniels said. “You see how hard he works ... Praying for Terry. He’s been there for me through a lot since I came into this league, the adverse times I went through last year and so far this year, and he’s been right by my side. I love Terry and appreciate him a lot.”

text:
The news that Philadelphia Eagles star Jalen Hurts has a likely season-ending injury of blood clots has sparked questions about how the condition developed in one of the NFL's top quarterbacks.

Hurts, 28, was diagnosed earlier this month with a superficial blood clot in his leg that then traveled to his lungs, developing into deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, the Eagles said Monday in a joint statement with Hurts' agent.

A diagnosis of bilateral pulmonary emboli -- meaning there are blood clots on both Hurts' right and left lungs -- can be serious, potentially causing permanent damage to the lung, low oxygen levels in the blood and damage to other organs in the body from not getting enough oxygen.

Hurts is currently on blood thinner medication, which prevents him from playing football, according to the Eagles. The team did not provide a timeline for Hurts' potential return to the field.

Here is a timeline of Hurts' injury, according to statements provided by the Eagles organization.

Timeline of Hurts' injury

Sunday, Oct. 4 -- Hurts is "cleated" during a game against the Los Angeles Rams in Philadelphia.

Wednesday, Oct. 7 -- Hurts practices in full with Eagles team.

Thursday, Oct. 8 -- Hurts practices in full with Eagles team. After practice, he informs the Eagles' medical staff that he was cleated during the Rams game and receives treatment for a calf injury.

Friday, Oct. 9 -- Hurts receives medical treatment and practices in full with the team.

Friday, Oct. 9 into Saturday, Oct. 10 -- Hurts flies to London with Eagles team.

Saturday, Oct. 10 -- Hurts undergoes an ultrasound that reveals a superficial blood clot.

Sunday, Oct. 11 -- Sources told ESPN that Hurts was hospitalized in London until 4 a.m. on Sunday. He then plays in the Eagles' 17-19 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Hurts and the team fly home immediately following the loss.

Monday, Oct. 12 -- Hurts receives medical treatment.

Tuesday, Oct. 13 -- Hurts receives medical treatment.

Wednesday, Oct. 14 -- Hurts practices in full with the team. A follow-up ultrasound done in the evening shows movement in the small blood clot.

Thursday, Oct. 15 -- Eagles announce Hurts will not play in Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.

Sunday, Oct. 18 -- Hurts is absent from the sidelines of the Eagles' loss to the Panthers.

Monday, Oct. 19 -- The Eagles and Hurts' agent announce the quarterback has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, and is taking blood thinner medication. As a result, he will be sidelined for an indefinite amount of time.

Deep vein thrombosis, or DVT, is when a blood clot develops in the deep veins, usually in the legs. A pulmonary embolism, or PE, occurs when a part of the DVT clot breaks off and travels to the lungs, which can be life-threatening, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

text:
Travis Kelce's brief exit from the Kansas City Chiefs' 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 18 sparked a debate about player safety after a tackle by Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley left the veteran tight end dealing with an ankle injury.

The incident occurred during the opening offensive drive at Arrowhead Stadium. Kelce went down after contact, appeared uncomfortable as he left the field and received medical attention on the sideline. The tackle immediately drew attention from Chiefs supporters watching the game.

The reaction intensified when fans questioned why officials had not penalized Henley for what they believed was an illegal hip-drop tackle. However, criticism of the play does not establish that a rule was broken, and no confirmed disciplinary action against the Chargers had been announced in the reporting reviewed as of Oct. 19.

Kelce returns after receiving treatment for his ankle

Kelce injured his right ankle during Kansas City's opening offensive drive after the Chiefs returned from their bye week. He went to the sideline for treatment and had the ankle taped.

The tight end returned for Kansas City's next possession and finished with 4 receptions for 53 yards in the 22–6 victory.

Afterward, Andy Reid said Kelce had tweaked his ankle and continued playing. The coach expected some soreness the following day.

Daiyan Henley faces criticism over the tackle

Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley became the focus of online criticism after bringing Kelce to the ground. Some viewers believed the tackle resembled a hip-drop technique, which the NFL has prohibited because of its potential to cause serious lower-body injuries.

The disputed play prompted calls for the league to review the contact and consider whether additional discipline was warranted. Some fans argued that the absence of an on-field flag allowed a potentially dangerous tackle to go unpunished.

However, the distinction between a forceful tackle and an illegal hip-drop tackle depends on the defender's specific movements. The fact that Kelce sustained an injury does not, by itself, establish that Henley committed a foul or deliberately acted improperly.

Why NFL fans are demanding punishment

The reaction centered on concerns that the league's restrictions on hip-drop tackles should apply consistently, regardless of the players involved. Supporters argued that an injury scare involving a high-profile star deserved closer scrutiny from officials and league decision-makers.

Posts on social media criticized the lack of a penalty, with some fans calling for the Chargers to face consequences. Others questioned whether the NFL's efforts to discourage dangerous tackling techniques were being enforced consistently during live games.

Those reactions reflect fan frustration, not an official league finding. The NFL would need to assess the actual tackle against its rules before determining whether a player should face a fine or another disciplinary measure.

What the NFL's hip-drop tackle rule prohibits

The NFL's rule applies when a defender grabs a runner with 1 or both hands, or wraps him with both arms, and then unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips or lower body, landing on or trapping the runner's legs at or below the knee.

The penalty is 15 yards and an automatic first down. An injury or awkward landing alone does not establish that the prohibited technique occurred.

Fans questioned whether Henley's tackle met that definition. The relevant movements, rather than the injury alone, determine whether the rule applies.

Kelce returned and helped the Chiefs secure victory

Despite the initial concern, Kelce returned to the field and contributed to Kansas City's offensive effort. His 4 catches for 53 yards helped the Chiefs maintain their advantage during a game in which their defense also played a significant role.

Kansas City won 22-6, improving to 5-0 and maintaining its position as the AFC's only unbeaten team entering the matchup. The Chargers, meanwhile, fell to 0-6 after struggling to turn offensive opportunities into touchdowns.

Kelce's return offered some immediate reassurance, but it does not establish the full extent of any ankle injury. The team's subsequent medical assessments and injury reports would provide a clearer indication of whether the incident could affect his availability for upcoming games.

Andy Reid and the Chiefs face questions about player safety

For Kansas City, the immediate priority is ensuring Kelce remains healthy as the season progresses. The tight end's importance to Mahomes and the offense makes his recovery a significant concern, particularly as the team aims to sustain its unbeaten run.

Head coach Andy Reid and the Chiefs' medical staff will be responsible for monitoring Kelce's condition and managing his workload as needed. Any decision about his availability should be based on medical evaluations rather than on assumptions about how he looked after his return to play.

The incident also raises a broader question facing NFL coaches: how can defenders tackle aggressively without resorting to techniques that put opponents at unnecessary risk? The league's rules establish boundaries, but their effectiveness depends on consistent enforcement and players understanding what constitutes prohibited contact.

Could Henley face an NFL fine?

The NFL can fine a player for prohibited contact even when officials did not flag the play during the game. Postgame discipline is separate from the enforcement of on-field penalties.

The league's 2026 fine schedule lists $17,911 for a first hip-drop tackle offense and $23,882 for a second offense. Players can appeal a fine through the league's disciplinary process.

Henley's tackle drew scrutiny because of its apparent resemblance to the prohibited technique. Fan criticism does not determine the outcome of a league review.

Reid has addressed Kelce's ankle injury

Andy Reid said after the Chargers game that Kelce had tweaked his ankle and continued playing. He expected the tight end to experience some soreness the following day.

Kelce returned after sideline treatment and finished Kansas City's 22–6 victory. His participation ahead of the next game will provide further information about his availability.

The tackle also drew criticism from viewers who believed Kelce used a prohibited technique, bringing the NFL's hip-drop rule into the discussion.

Fun fact: Travis Kelce once considered pursuing professional baseball after being suspended for the 2010 college football season, but his older brother, Jason, encouraged him to return to football.

TL;DR

Travis Kelce suffered an apparent ankle injury after a tackle by Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley on Oct. 18.

Kelce returned to the game and finished with 4 catches for 53 yards.

Fans criticized the lack of a penalty, arguing the tackle appeared to resemble an illegal hip-drop technique.

The NFL's hip-drop rule carries a 15-yard penalty and an automatic first down when a violation is called.

No confirmed fine or suspension related to the tackle had been established in the reporting reviewed as of Oct. 19.

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles were hit with their worst-case scenario on Monday when it was revealed quarterback Jalen Hurts was out for the rest of the season after doctors discovered blood clots in his lungs.

Little was known about Hurts’ condition when the news initially dropped, and former Pro Bowl fullback turned NFL Network analyst Michael Robinson even doubted whether Hurts’ medical situation was as dire as it was being made out to be.

“It looked like they were trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts just so that they could have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts,” Robinson stated during an appearance on “NFL Gameday Kickoff” on Thursday. “And, again, I’m not saying I know nothing, guys.

“But if I’m just playing devil’s advocate here, and I’m thinking that way, if I’m Jalen Hurts — or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp — I’m saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season … he’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.”

Robinson Walks Back Jalen Hurts Take

After news came out on Monday that Hurts required three months of treatment to fix his blood clot issue, social media was quick to remind Robinson how off base he was with his comments.

The polarizing analyst then took to social media to issue an apology for accusing Hurts of milking an injury he didn’t think was serious.

“My official apology to @JalenHurts, @Eagles, and the entire fanbase. My comments were wrong. No excuse,” Robinson posted on X.

“I want to sincerely apologize to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organization and fan base for my comments last Thursday. They were unfounded and I never should’ve speculated on a health issue of a player nor his commitment to his team.”

Jalen Hurts’ Agent Reveals Details of His Recovery

With the three-month timeline given to Hurts for treatment, it would sideline him through mid-January, by which the Eagles’ season very well could be over.

Not many details were known about what Hurts’ recovery looked like until his agent Nicole Lynn provided some clarity on that on social media.

“Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts,” Lynn wrote. “In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.

“Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. “blood thinners”). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

“Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery.”

text:
The Chicago Bears have put out their first injury report of the week ahead of the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots.

Because the Bears play on Thursday night this week, the first injury report comes out on Monday, and it's just an estimation because the Bears did not hold an actual practice and instead conducted a walkthrough.

The three biggest names we're keeping an eye on this week are running back Kyle Monangai, right guard Jonah Jackson and linebacker T.J. Edwards.

Now, a look at the Bears' full injury report for Monday

Bears' Monday injury report

Monangai, Edwards and Jackson injury updates

The three most important players on the list, Monangai, Edwards and Jackson, were all estimated non-participants, which leaves them in a lackluster spot to begin the week.

We know Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury that has kept him out for two games in a row. Monangai was initially labeled as week-to-week and he has not practiced since coming down with his injury.

Edwards missed his first game of the season in Week 6 with the hamstring issue, and Jackson exited the win over the Atlanta Falcons early with his hip and quadriceps injuries.

On Monday, offensive coordinator Press Taylor did not offer an update on the Bears' right guard.

"We'll see where Jonah's at and if he's got a chance to play on Thursday night," he said. "But we're excited about the depth we have there.

We're skeptical all three will suit up in Week 7 because it is a short week, which means each player has less time to get right.

If Jackson sits, fellow guard Luke Newman figures to take over for him after the former sixth-round pick was called into duty when Jackson got injured on Sunday.

The Bears will likely continue to roll with running back Roschon Johnson if Monangai is absent again, and linebacker D'Marco Jackson will start in place of Edwards.

More injury updates

Linebacker Jack Sanborn is a new addition to the injury report. There was no news from the team during the game about his concussion, so he amounts to a surprise.

After sitting out in Week 6, both cornerback Tyrique Stevenson and rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott were both upgraded, which puts them on track to return. Stevenson logged only limited practices last week, while Elliott did not practice at all.

The Bears will drop their second injury report of the week on Tuesday, and it won't be an estimate because the Bears will conduct a regular practice.

text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — Washington Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin was taken off the field on a cart after an injury to his left knee that the team fears could be serious.

McLaurin was running a pattern in the first quarter Monday night against the San Francisco 49ers when he went down with the injury. His knee appeared to buckle as he tried to get free from cornerback Deommodore Lenoir.

McLaurin stayed down while teammates knelt nearby before he was driven off the field. He was immediately ruled out for the game.

“The concern now is that it could be significant,” coach Dan Quinn said after the Commanders' 23-17 loss. “We’ll do the scans (Tuesday) and give you an update. But that’s the concern tonight. It’s definitely something that there’s fear.”

The 31-year-old McLaurin has missed more than two games in a season only once since entering the league in 2019. He missed seven games last season while dealing with an injured quadriceps.

McLaurin has 15 catches for 230 yards and one touchdown this season, missing one game with an injured hamstring in Week 4.

He is a two-time Pro Bowler and has 513 catches for 7,191 yards and 42 touchdowns in his career.

The Commanders also lost defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw to a knee injury late in the first half, and he was ruled out for the game.

Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season saw a limited roster of Penn State alumni with Saquon Barkley and Tyler Warren out due to injury and Mike Gesicki on a bye week.

However, there were still good performances from those who did play, such as wide receiver Jahan Dotson’s touchdown catch and a pair of Jacksonville Jaguars appearing playing in London for the second straight week.

Here’s how the former Nittany Lions did in Week 6 of NFL action.

Jahan Dotson, wide receiver, Atlanta Falcons

Dotson was the only former Nittany Lion to get into the end zone, and it was by no means an easy reception.

The Atlanta Falcons were struggling in the passing game against the Chicago Bears throughout the first half until over halfway through the second quarter, when quarterback Michael Penix Jr. connected with Dotson for a touchdown.

From the Bears’ 13-yard line, Dotson ran a fade route under heavy man coverage by cornerback Malik Muhammad II. Penix threw the ball to Dotson’s back shoulder, and the former Penn Stater caught it and kept himself in bounds for his second touchdown of the season.

Dotson closed the game with a team-high 87 receiving yards on only three catches. He was only targeted five times throughout the game, with his longest catch being 41 yards.

Dotson’s performance wasn’t enough, as Chicago defeated Atlanta, 31-23.

Tyler Warren, tight end, Indianapolis Colts

Warren has been dealing with a groin injury and was placed on the injury report Friday as a game-time decision ahead of the Indianapolis Colts’ matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

He previously injured his groin in a preseason joint practice with the Falcons on Aug. 19 and didn’t return to the field.

Warren ended up sitting out on Sunday, and the Titans beat the Colts, 26-20. Will Mallory, Pharaoh Brown and Mo Alie-Cox played in Warren’s stead.

The former Nittany Lion still paces Indianapolis with 30 receptions and two touchdowns, while ranking third on the team with 213 receiving yards.

Brenton Strange, wide receiver Jacksonville Jaguars

Brenton Strange was a solid contributor in Jacksonville's 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans on Sunday at Wembley Stadium.

It didn’t take long for Strange to make his presence felt. On the first play of the game, quarterback Trevor Lawrence found Strange up the middle for a 24-yard gain.

Strange closed the game with five catches for 44 yards on seven targets, averaging 8.8 yards per reception.

However, Strange took a holding penalty on what would’ve been running back Bhayshul Tuten’s first touchdown of the game. It was called back, and two plays later Lawrence’s pass was picked off in the end zone by Calen Bullock.

Strange’s 6-yard catch with under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter set kicker Cam Little up for a game-tying 60-yard field goal.

Parker Washington, wide receiver Jacksonville Jaguars

While Strange was a consistent backup option, Parker Washington was Lawrence’s most targeted receiver, even though many of those targets didn’t result in anything.

Although Washington had 64 receiving yards on the day, he only had four catches on 11 targets, including three straight passes in the first quarter where Lawrence’s ball placement was off.

However, when Washington did catch the ball cleanly, he was highly efficient, averaging 16 yards per reception.

Washington’s longest catch of the day was a 27-yarder in the second quarter to set up Tuten’s rushing touchdown to tie the game, 7-7.

KeAndre Lambert-Smith, wide receiver, Los Angeles Chargers

As the Los Angeles Chargers faced a third-and-1 on the Kansas City Chiefs’ 37-yard line down 19-6 in the fourth quarter, quarterback Justin Herbert threw a screen pass to former Penn State wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

But Lambert-Smith was stripped of the ball by cornerback L’Jarius Sneed. It was recovered by linebacker Drue Tranquill, and the Chargers’ comeback hopes were dashed.

Lambert-Smith finished the game with five catches for 32 yards on nine targets. He was Herbert’s top receiving target and had the second-most receiving yards, only trailing wide receiver Quentin Johnston’s singular 57-yard reception.

text:
Rams receiver Davante Adams will be out for six to 10 weeks with a significant hamstring injury, Los Angeles coach Sean McVay said Monday.

The Rams (2-4) also lost veteran defensive tackle Poona Ford for the season due to a ruptured triceps, and defensive tackle Kobie Turner is going on injured reserve with a groin injury amid a cascade of health setbacks for the struggling preseason Super Bowl favorites, who have lost three of four.

Adams, a six-time Pro Bowl selection and the NFL's leader in touchdown catches last season, apparently got hurt on the Rams' penultimate offensive snap in their embarrassing 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The injury happened on a noncontact play, with Adams pulling up in the end zone and hobbling to the sideline.

The 33-year-old Adams has 30 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns this season, his 13th in the NFL. He missed three games late last season with a hamstring injury, but returned for the playoffs.

"It's significant when you don't have a player like Davante, but we have to be able to adjust," McVay said. "His contributions can't be measured. You don't replace somebody like him, and so what you've got to do is you've got to be able to figure out what's the next right thing? What does that look like in terms of our vision? We'll have to adjust and adapt."

Adams' injury is particularly significant to the Rams because they don't have a trusted No. 3 receiver on their roster behind him and All-Pro Puka Nacua. Konata Mumpfield's eight catches for 127 yards are the third-most for a Rams wide receiver this season.

Los Angeles also didn't have an effective No. 3 wideout last season, and Matthew Stafford threw to his depth receivers with less frequency than any other quarterback on a playoff team.

Ford is a nine-year NFL veteran in his second season with the Rams. He has played just under 40% of their defensive snaps this season as a space-filling lineman alongside Turner and Aaron Donald.

Turner is on the field much more frequently than Ford for the Rams, but the fourth-year pro with 22 tackles this season will also miss "a handful of games," McVay said.

McVay confirmed new kicker Blake Grupe is out for the season after tearing a ligament in his knee while making a tackle on kickoff coverage. The Rams will have to sign their third kicker of the season before they visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

McVay said star cornerback Trent McDuffie is "feeling much better" after missing Sunday's game with an injury picked up in practice late last week. The Rams won't determine whether McDuffie will play against the Raiders until later in the week.

The question during Monday's OutKick meeting went as follows: Did Michael Robinson just give the worst-aged sports take in history?

It happened Thursday on NFL Network, when the former fullback suggested that Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was faking an injury so as not to be the fall guy for a losing team.

"He's pulling himself out, so this doesn't look like it's on me," Robinson said.

EAGLES QUARTERBACK JALEN HURTS RULED OUT OF SUNDAY'S GAME 'OUT OF AN ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION' DUE TO BLOOD CLOT

On October 4, Hurts was cleated in the calf against the Rams. Six days later, an ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. He still played against the Jaguars the following day in London, despite doctors reportedly keeping him awake all night over concerns about the risks associated with sleeping with a blood clot. On October 15, the Eagles released a statement saying Hurts wouldn't play Sunday against the Panthers.

That night, Robinson chucked his now-infamous verbal air ball.

"If I'm Jalen Hurts or anybody in the Jalen Hurts' camp, I'm saying 'if everybody is hurt, then I'm hurt, too'," he said, referring to the rash of injuries on the Eagles roster.

Robinson added: "I would advise all of our viewers to go Google 'superficial blood clot' as opposed to a real blood clot."

EAGLES APPEAR SET TO ADD QB FROM COWBOYS' PRACTICE SQUAD AS JALEN HURTS DEALS WITH BLOOD CLOT

Well, it turns out Hurts' condition was far more serious than Robinson suggested. Doctors subsequently discovered blood clots in his lungs — and now he's expected to miss the rest of the season. Part of me wondered if Robinson's season as a broadcaster was in jeopardy as well, although he did issue the following apology Monday night."

"I want to sincerely apologize to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organization and fan base for my comments last Thursday. They were unfounded and I never should've speculated on a health issue of a player nor his commitment to this team."

The mea culpa seems sincere — and boy was it necessary.

I will admit that my favorite key on my laptop is delete. It's rare that I have to come up with an opinion on a hot mic. But to imply that a world-class athlete is exaggerating an injury to preserve his reputation is a staggering lapse in judgment.

On the off chance that Robinson was correct, he might have scored a day-long victory lap. But whiffing like that gave his credibility a permanent stain.

NBA GREAT SAYS HE NEARLY 'DROPPED DEAD' DUE TO BLOOD CLOT AS HE OFFERS ADVICE TO VICTOR WEMBANYAMA

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Don't get me wrong, there have been a lot of bad sports opinions that had little impact on the pundit's career. In 2016, Max Kellerman said that Tom Brady was about to "fall off a cliff," only to watch the QB win three more Super Bowls. In 2014, Skip Bayless said that Johnny Manziel was going to be bigger in Cleveland than LeBron James ever was. In 2010, Mel Kiper Jr. said he would retire from ESPN if Jimmy Clausen — who went 1-13 in the 14 NFL games he started — was not a successful quarterback. And last month, LA Times columnist Bill Plaschke said that this year's Rams would go undefeated en route to the Super Bowl (they are 2-4).

But none of those takes attacked a man's character the way Robinson attacked Hurts'. They might have been ridiculous, but they were also harmless.

Look, I don't want to see Robinson lose his gig the way some online angry villagers do. He gave an egregious opinion, but one reckless remark shouldn't erase a career's worth of work.

This one is going to stick with the former Seahawk for a while, though, even with the apology. Bad predictions are forgotten. Baseless accusations aren't.

Six games into the 2026 NFL season, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix ranks 32nd in the NFL with an average of 5.6 yards per passing attempt.

Nix's struggles and inability (or unwillingness) to throw the ball downfield have been well-documented this season, and the QB was asked about it following the team's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks last Thursday.

“I don’t understand why we can’t really push the ball vertically right now," Nix said. "Defenses are just sitting back there hanging out. We’re just going to keep running the football. Hopefully you have to find ways to get more out of it.”

Some fans and pundits have speculated that Nix's struggles are related to the ankle injury Nix suffered during the NFL playoffs last season. Not so much the physical fallout, but Nix's ability to get over the injury mentally.

When asked if Nix is struggling to mentally move past his injury during his Monday conference call, Broncos coach Sean Payton essentially sidestepped the question, saying the QB has done a good job overcoming adversity in his career.

"All the other things relative to the mental toughness, the mental fortitude — this is a tough league," Payton said. "We hit every aspect, and I think that’s one of the things that attracted us to Bo in the beginning is we had seen his ability to climb through adversity. It’s not just Bo that feels that. Right now, offensively, I feel that, our players feel that and we’ll improve.”

Publicly, Payton didn't suggest Nix is struggling to get over his injury mentally. Meanwhile, somebody (presumably within the organization) has leaked to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video that the club believes Nix is playing "a bit gun shy."

"[T]here is a difference with Nix in 2026, where Nix is focused on not losing the game more than winning the game," Palmer tweeted on Monday. "Don't turn the ball over. Don't be the reason why we lose the game. That's kind of manifested in his mind to the point that the conservative approach has become an issue on the field."

Palmer's lengthy tweet also included this:

Nix is healthy, and the ankle is fine. But returning from an injury is also not cut and dry and takes time. The Broncos want Nix to run it more and they're seeing a player that is a bit gun shy right now. If you look at the runs that Denver has dialed up, a lot of them he's looking for the sidelines and he's looking for a way to get down as soon as possible. He's not looking for the extra yards or the needed yards in key situations. It's been frustrating.

Palmer later suggested that Nix is "seeing ghosts at times," and the team is "obviously concerned with the funk he's currently stuck in." And this is perhaps the most notable part of the report: "They'd love to see him take a couple of big hits and realize he's not going to get hurt, the ankle is good, remember you're a tough football player."

Assuming Palmer's information came straight from the team, that seems to be an admission that the club believes Nix is in his head about coming back from last season's ankle injury. That's not surprising, given that many fans and pundits came to the same conclusion.

This week, Nix will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that allows 8.6 yards per passing attempt, most in the NFL. Palmer noted that "one big game" could get Nix going again. Fans in Denver can only hope that Nix gets back on track and regains his confidence in Arizona this week.

text:
Mike Evans departed the 49ers’ game against the Washington Commanders Monday night before halftime with an Achilles injury, further depleting a wide receiver corps that was already thin.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans’ injury is the same soreness he had dealt with throughout the week, and the 49ers don’t believe he will be out long-term.

The free-agent signee was seen stretching his lower legs shortly before his final catch of the half. On that play, Evans looped behind Washington linebacker Sonny Styles after lining up in the slot and caught a low pass from Purdy, going to the ground.

He stayed down a few seconds, then got up with a hand from Commanders defenders and walked to the 49ers’ locker room with a team trainer. He was ruled out for the game just after halftime.

“It’s bothered him throughout the week. With his Achilles tendinitis, it flared up tonight,” Shanahan said. “Hope he recovers through the week and I don’t think it’s a long-term thing. It cost him this game for two quarters and hopefully he can play next week; if not, the rest of the group has to step up.”

Evans was questionable to play Monday with Achilles tightness and rib issues. He has played through rib pain the last several weeks after fracturing several ribs.

Already missing were Ricky Pearsall (season-ending knee surgery), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (calf).

The six-time Pro Bowl receiver had three catches for 94 yards in the first half before leaving the game, including a 54-yard catch-and-run.

Evans, 33, was a key to the 49ers’ win last week in Seattle, connecting with Brock Purdy for 75 yards on a single fourth-quarter drive to help swing the game. He was clearly playing through pain in that game, and continued to look ginger Monday at Levi’s Stadium.

Evans came to the 49ers from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the offseason on a three-year, $42.4 million contract. He entered Monday’s game with 24 catches for 326 yards and three touchdowns.

Washington also lost its top receiver in the game as Terry McLaurin went down clutching his knee late in the first quarter running a route along the left sideline. He was carted off the field to the Commanders’ locker room.

“It was just the same thing that was bothering him all week,” Shanahan said. “It acted up too much during the game and he couldn’t go. We’ll see how he feels this week.”

When asked if it was a “close call” whether to allow Evans to play with his injury, Shanahan said Evans’ inability to finish the game didn’t come as a surprise.

“It was a pretty close call in terms of he wasn’t able to (practice) all week,” Shanahan said. “It’s something he’s dealt with in the past in his career. He felt confident he’d be good today. So that was the confidence he gave me. But we knew he might not be able to last.”

Evans was playing his third straight game with two broken ribs, but he appeared on the injury report last week with his new Achilles injury. Before he exited Monday, Evans continued his stellar debut season with the 49ers.

The six-time Pro Bowl selection had three catches for 94 yards, including a 54-yard catch-and-run to set up the 49ers’ second touchdown that provided a 13-3 lead in the first quarter. Evans has 27 catches for 420 yards and three touchdowns in six games this season.

Without Evans, the 49ers finished with four available wide receivers: Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Malik Turner, who was elevated from the practice squad Monday. Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple games after he was injured in a win against the Seahawks on Oct. 11. Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) are on injured reserve.

Special teams troubles: Following Christian McCaffrey’s first-quarter touchdown run, Eddy Piñeiro missed the extra point. It continued an odd trend for the 49ers' kicker, who has missed seven extra points across the past two seasons but has missed just four field goals.

Shanahan was blunt when asked about his level of concern with Piñeiro.

“Yeah. I mean, he’s got to make them,” Shanahan said. “He missed another one today and fortunately it didn’t get us, but I think everyone knows the answer to that. You’ve got to make your extra points.”

Piñeiro has missed three field-goal attempts this season. He missed just one in 2025, which helped him earn a four-year, $17 million contract extension during the offseason.

Another special teamer drawing unwanted attention: punt returner Jacob Cowing. The 25-year-old let a punt in the first quarter slip right through his hands. He recovered the ball, but the 49ers were forced to start that drive on their 4-yard line.

“Jake made a real bad decision on (that) one,” Shanahan said, added Cowing “had to let it go” into the end zone. “I don’t think he made a mistake on any of the others, but yeah, that was a bad decision by him.”

Shanahan’s words offered a shift in tone from a week ago, when Cowing also muffed a punt against the Seahawks and he said: “No, it wasn’t enough (to bench him). It’s something that he can’t do … but no, we’re not changing his position yet.”

Other injuries: Linebacker Luke Gifford (groin) and nickelback Upton Stout (shoulder) exited Monday night’s game and did not return.

Gifford filled in against the Commanders for Garret Wallow, who was out with a hamstring injury, and exited in the first half. Wallow, a rotational linebacker behind Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw, will likely be out through the 49ers’ bye week, which comes after their next game in Atlanta. Greenlaw missed Monday’s game due to a suspension; rookie Jaden Dugger played in Greenlaw’s place.

Stout has been recovering from an AC joint sprain that he suffered Week 4 against the Broncos. He played the previous two games but has been limited during the week. Stout aggravated the injury Monday night. In his place, the 49ers put reserve safety Ashtyn Davis in the slot. Davis picked up an illegal contact penalty in the fourth quarter.

Superstar edge-rusher Myles Garrett was already on injured reserve, star cornerback Trent McDuffie missed Sunday's game with a groin issue and Monday's injury report hit hard beyond just Adams:

The Rams were already having surprising issues on offense. The loss of Adams will not alleviate them.

The 33-year-old was having an excellent season, catching 30 passes for 480 yards and four scores while giving the Rams one of the most dynamic wideout duos in the league alongside Puka Nacua.

Now, an offense already heavily reliant on Nacua will need to lean on him even more heavily. The Rams could also turn to a trade or free agency to bolster the position behind him.

But the Rams have now gone from winning the offseason to potentially missing out on the playoffs altogether. There's plenty of season left, but L.A. has quickly become one of the most injury-impacted teams in football. Somebody on the offense beyond Nacua, Matt Stafford and (the suddenly disgruntled) Kyren Williams will need to pick up some of the slack.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury.

text:
The Washington Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin early Monday night after he went down with what appears to be a significant knee injury.

McLaurin was running a route near the end of the first quarter of Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers when he suddenly fell near the sideline at Levi's Stadium. Replay showed that McLaurin's left knee gave out on him and buckled as he was planting to the outside.

He remained down on the field for quite some time in front of the Commanders' bench, clearly in a lot of pain.

A cart eventually came out for McLaurin, and he hopped up and onto the vehicle under his own power with his entire left leg in a full air cast. Players from both teams then saw him off.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury. Head coach Dan Quinn said after the contest that they didn't have any details, but they were concerned that the injury was significant.

McLaurin had one catch for 27 yards in the contest before he went down.

McLaurin entered Monday with 203 receiving yards and a single touchdown in four games this season, his eighth in the league with the Commanders. He missed the team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury he suffered at practice before that contest before returning the following week.

While it's unclear how long McLaurin may be sidelined, the injury is a tough sign for a Commanders group that is struggling this season. The Commanders sit at just 1-4-1, which has them in last in the NFC East race. While they rallied a bit late and had a good look at the win down the stretch on Monday night, they couldn't quite pull it off.

The win pushed the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 on the year, which is the best record in the league. Only two other teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, are also still undefeated.

The NFC East is still wide open, so the Commanders aren't completely out of the playoff hunt yet despite their rough start. But losing a target like McLaurin for a substantial amount of time is going to make things much more difficult for quarterback Jayden Daniels as they approach the midway point of the season.

title: NFL Network: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts likely out for rest of 2026 season due to blood clots
description:

The Philadelphia Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released a statement on Monday, relaying that doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs.

text:
Jalen Hurts' season is likely over.

The Philadelphia Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released a statement on Monday, relaying that doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts is now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season as he undergoes treatment, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday.

Hurts' recovery is expected to take three months, Rapoport and Schefter added, putting his return this season in doubt.

“Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition,” the Eagles and Lynn said in a statement.

“Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

“Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

“We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery.”

The Eagles initially ruled out Hurts on Oct. 15 for Philadelphia's Week 6 game against the Panthers, and then placed the QB on injured reserve on Saturday.

In their original statement last week, the Eagles announced that Hurts first reported issues with his calf on Oct. 8 after he was cleated during Philadelphia's Week 4 loss to the Rams on Oct. 4. Hurts received treatment and was added to the Eagles' injury report on Oct. 9 as a full practice participant ahead of their trip to London for last Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

A "superficial blood clot" was revealed during an evaluation on Oct. 10 in London, but the Eagles said that medical staff and doctors determined that "Jalen could safely play" against Jacksonville.

A subsequent follow-up exam on Wednesday "revealed movement in the small blood clot," which led to him being ruled out for their game against Carolina.

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni was asked on Monday if there was something he felt the team could have done differently regarding Hurts' status.

“I’m not a medical expert," Sirianni said. "I lean on our guys in all those situations. I’m a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every single situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It’s not just me that has major care for our players. It’s them as well. We are all there, and I’m glad to be part of an organization that cares about the guys the way our guys do.”

The Eagles currently sit at 2-4 but are in second place in the NFC East. Backup Tanner McKee started the Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The 26-year-old struggled to move the offense until the end of the double-digit defeat.

text:
The Washington Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin early Monday night after he went down with what appears to be a significant knee injury.

McLaurin was running a route near the end of the first quarter of Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers when he suddenly fell near the sideline at Levi's Stadium. Replay showed that McLaurin's left knee gave out on him and buckled as he was planting to the outside.

He remained down on the field for quite some time in front of the Commanders' bench, clearly in a lot of pain.

A cart eventually came out for McLaurin, and he hopped up and onto the vehicle under his own power with his entire left leg in a full air cast. Players from both teams then saw him off.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury. Head coach Dan Quinn said after the contest that they didn't have any details, but they were concerned that the injury was significant.

McLaurin had one catch for 27 yards in the contest before he went down.

McLaurin entered Monday with 203 receiving yards and a single touchdown in four games this season, his eighth in the league with the Commanders. He missed the team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury he suffered at practice before that contest before returning the following week.

While it's unclear how long McLaurin may be sidelined, the injury is a tough sign for a Commanders group that is struggling this season. The Commanders sit at just 1-4-1, which has them in last in the NFC East race. While they rallied a bit late and had a good look at the win down the stretch on Monday night, they couldn't quite pull it off.

The win pushed the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 on the year, which is the best record in the league. Only two other teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, are also still undefeated.

The NFC East is still wide open, so the Commanders aren't completely out of the playoff hunt yet despite their rough start. But losing a target like McLaurin for a substantial amount of time is going to make things much more difficult for quarterback Jayden Daniels as they approach the midway point of the season.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- After playing through Achilles soreness for most of the first half of Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders, San Francisco 49ers receiver Mike Evans departed just before halftime because of an Achilles injury.

The 49ers initially labeled Evans as questionable to return but ruled him out early in the third quarter. They went on to win, 23-17.

"Same thing that was bothering him all week," coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game. "Acted up too much in the game and couldn't go. We'll see how he feels this week."

Shanahan added that he doesn't believe Evans will need additional testing on the Achilles.

With 1:10 left in the second quarter, Evans caught a 16-yard in-breaker from quarterback Brock Purdy. After Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves touched him down, Evans stayed on the field and stretched his right leg.

Niners medical personnel ran on the field, helped Evans up and then supported him as he slowly walked back to the locker room.

Evans did not practice all week because of an ongoing recovery from broken ribs and a sore Achilles. He had a questionable tag entering the game, with Shanahan saying after the game that it was a close call on whether he'd play.

"We knew he might not be able to last," the coach said.

Evans had three catches for 94 yards before exiting.

Without Evans, the only healthy Niners receivers available were Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and Malik Turner.

"Obviously having him out there, he's a Hall of Famer," Purdy told ESPN after the game.

"But I thought our guys stepped. We still got to find a way to make plays."

text:
One of Oklahoma’s rookies was involved in a scary situation on Sunday.

Linebacker Kendal Daniels, who spent the 2025 season at Oklahoma, suffered a neck injury in the Atlanta Falcons’ game against the Chicago Bears. Daniels made a low tackle on Bears tight end Colston Loveland before staying on the ground for several minutes.

Daniels was eventually carted off the field and taken to a local hospital in Atlanta. The Falcons later reported on X (formerly Twitter) that Daniels was “alert” and had movement in all his extremities.

After the game, which Atlanta lost 31-23, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski revealed that the team had received “all positive news” about the rookie linebacker.

Before suffering his injury, Daniels made a key impact in the game. He logged seven tackles, six of which were solo stops, and also notched a tackle for loss.

Daniels, a fourth-round selection in the 2026 NFL Draft, has already registered 29 total tackles and 22 solo tackles during his rookie season.

In his lone season at Oklahoma, Daniels was a key piece on OU’s defense, finishing 2025 with 53 tackles and nine tackles for loss in 13 starts. He began his college career at Oklahoma State.

Sooner rookies log strong showings

Rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas didn’t light up the stat sheet on Sunday, but he played a key role in the Kansas City Chiefs’ win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Thomas hit Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert in the red zone, forcing him to throw an incompletion. Thomas’ hit nearly forced Herbert to fumble, but the veteran signal caller was able to throw the ball forward and avoid the turnover.

The former Oklahoma edge rusher appeared on 33 snaps and logged a 63.9 Pro Football Focus (PFF) defensive grade.

Thomas was a star throughout his four seasons in Norman. He ended his college career with 65 tackles, 25.5 tackles for loss, 17 sacks, four forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries and a scoop-and-score touchdown.

The Chiefs selected Thomas with the No. 40 overall pick (second round) in the 2026 NFL Draft. Thomas has played on 178 snaps so far in his rookie season.

Wide receiver Deion Burks had his best game as a professional on Sunday.

Burks, a former Sooner playing with the Indianapolis Colts, logged a 36-yard reception in his game against the Tennessee Titans. He finished the 26-20 loss with two catches for 41 yards, and he also rushed once for seven yards.

The Colts picked Burks in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Burks spent his final two college seasons in Norman after transferring from Purdue.

Williams shines in first game back

Baker Mayfield and Jalen Hurts are both injured, and Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings had the week off.

That made Caleb Williams, who spent only one season at OU, the only Sooner quarterback in action on Sunday.

Williams led the Bears to their eight-point win over the Falcons. He completed 30 of his 36 pass attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown.

Williams had missed the Bears’ last three games with a leg injury before returning on Saturday. He led Chicago to the playoffs in 2025.

Before becoming an NFL star, Williams began his college days at OU, where he became the Sooners’ starting quarterback midway through the 2021 season. Williams, though, followed coach Lincoln Riley to USC after only one year in Norman.

At just 28 years old, and only 20 months removed from being named the Super Bowl MVP, Jalen Hurts is now on blood thinners to stave off what – without them – could be life-threatening blood clots in his lungs.

The Associated Press and others are reporting that the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback won’t play again this season, which would appear an obvious outcome since treatment for Hurts’ injuries – bilateral pulmonary emboli and deep vein thrombosis in medical jargon – requires three months on the blood thinners.

That much everyone can agree on. It is everything in between that makes the situation less cut-and-dry.

The Eagles, in conjunction with Hurts’ agent Nicole Lynn, have released two statements in the past four days detailing Hurts’ injury and treatment, citing the “interest of transparency.”

The timeline breaks down like this:

Left unanswered are two critical issues.

For starters, why was Hurts permitted to fly across the Atlantic twice? Along with injury, as in Hurts’ case, deep vein thrombosis can be caused by extended periods sitting on long flights, pulmonary critical care expert Dr. Parth Rali told CNN. The International Air Transport Association guidelines stipulate that “travelers with a recent DVT of the legs may fly once they are asymptomatic and stable on anticoagulants.”

A bigger question, though, is why was Hurts permitted to play in the game at all?

At best, he was coming off a handful of hours of rest after a stressful night in the hospital. At worst, he was competing with a serious medical condition.

During his normally scheduled Monday news conference, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not go into detail about either decision, only repeatedly saying that he trusted his medical team and that “it’s not just me that cares deeply about our players, it’s them as well.”

Sirianni added that this was the same medical team that “helped 21 of 22 guys be available for the Super Bowl.” Asked how Hurts was feeling, the coach said he would keep his private conversations private.

“But I haven’t been without him for an extended period of time,” Sirianni said. “I miss him.”

As Sirianni spoke on a live-streamed interview, the chat box down the right side of the video erupted with unanswered questions. Even before the announcement about Hurts, Sirianni and the Eagles were on a short leash with their notoriously hard-to-please fan base. Philadelphia has lost four games in a row, the team’s worst skid in Sirianni’s six seasons.

Along with the usual “fire Sirianni” suggestions, fans directed their ire at Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie and general manager Howie Roseman, who did not make themselves available for comment. Some called them cowards; others opted for more colorful language.

Most, however, questioned whether Hurts’ safety had been sacrificed in the name of the sport.

“Super Bowl MVP has been done wrong,” one wrote.

Added another, “Players’ health is at the forefront of our mind? Obviously not.”

Still another simply called the decision “shameful” and wondered who “put his life at risk.”

Deep vein thromboses, while rare, are not entirely uncommon among athletes. In February 2020, San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama was diagnosed with one in his shoulder, undergoing immediate surgery to prevent it from spreading to his lungs.

Week 6 wraps up in Santa Clara, where the Washington Commanders will visit the San Francisco 49ers for a "Monday Night Football" showdown. As Washington tries to inch closer to .500 on the season and rid itself of the sour taste of a tie with the Giants last week, it will have one of its key weapons on offense.

The status of Stefon Diggs was up in the air for this primetime matchup as the wideout dealt with a hamstring injury, but he is active. Diggs did not practice at the start of the week on Thursday, but returned to practice in a limited capacity on Friday and Saturday. Officially, he was listed as questionable.

Diggs, who signed a one-year deal with the franchise in early August, did not play in last week's tie with New York because of that hamstring.

49ers vs. Commanders prediction: Can San Francisco remain unbeaten? Full 'Monday Night Football' breakdown

Jared Dubin

When healthy, the 32-year-old has been a heavily involved figure within the Commanders offense, averaging just under eight targets per game so far this season. Because Terry McLaurin has also been in and out of the lineup due to injury, Diggs actually leads the team in targets (31), receptions (18), and receiving touchdowns (3). His 170 receiving yards are second to McLaurin (203).

What's fascinating about Diggs' tenure so far in Washington is that he's seen minimal time playing with quarterback Jayden Daniels. Because of injuries, there's only been one full game played between the two. That came in the season-opening loss to Philadelphia, where Diggs caught four of nine targets for 55 yards and a touchdown. Before Daniels left Week 2's loss to the Cowboys with a left elbow injury, the two connected for another touchdown. If/when these two can stay healthy and be on the field at the same time, they've flashed some explosiveness.

That'll be extremely important in this NFC matchup as the 49ers defense has been one of the stoutest in the league entering Week 6. San Francisco has the lowest explosive play rate allowed through five games by any team since 2000. Having a healthy Diggs would go a long way in putting a dent into that historic figure.

HOUSTON -- Texans wide receiver Tank Dell will return to the field against the New York Giants on Sunday after a 22-month hiatus, coach DeMeco Ryans announced Monday.

It will be the first game for Dell since the 2023 third-round pick missed all of the 2025 season after he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in the Texans' Week 16 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024.

"No huge expectations from what he needs to do," Ryans said. "I'm just going to be excited to see him just out there for the first time in over two years, just getting some game action. Dell started the 2026 season on injured reserve when Houston made its 53-man roster cuts. He wasn't on the physically unable to perform list to start training camp but throughout camp he took part only in individual drills.

text:
Injuries are piling up on top of losses for the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams.

Wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a hamstring injury in L.A.'s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday and is expected to miss six to 10 weeks, head coach Sean McVay told reporters Monday.

NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Adams is expected to have a procedure on his hamstring tendon to clean it out and the hope is he can return around the team's bye week or a little after. The Rams' bye falls on Week 11.

Adams, 33, was having another standout season for the Rams, with 30 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns while sporting a 16.0 yards-per-reception average, which would be the best in his career.

McVay announced a litany of injuries for the Rams in addition to Adams'.

Defensive tackle Poona Ford will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps muscle, as will recent addition, kicker Blake Grupe, due to a knee injury. DT Kobie Turner (groin) is headed to injured reserve, guaranteeing he'll miss a minimum of four weeks.

Myles Garrett, who has been on IR since having knee surgery after the team's Week 1 loss in Australia, also won't start practicing this week.

"The first thing is you feel terrible for these guys," McVay said. "Those guys are key contributors for us, so there's a lot of emotions. But the first thing is support these guys, be there for them, and then the next thing is make sure that we figure out what's the best way for our team to be able to move forward in the absence of some critical factors for us."

Through six weeks, Adams was the Rams' receiving yards leader and the only pass catcher with multiple TD receptions. Puka Nacua, the team leader with 37 receptions who missed two games earlier this year, will continue to play a major role in the operation, as will tight ends such as Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Terrance Ferguson could factor in eventually, as well, though he's not eligible to come off IR until Week 8. Wide receiver Konata Mumpfield flashed in one of the games Nacua missed, going for 93 yards and a score on four catches, and there's also Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell.

With Ford and Turner going down, plus Garrett not on the way back yet, the Rams have some work to do to fortify their front seven. Aaron Donald and Braden Fiske will be tasked with some heavy lifting alongside larger roles for Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison, the latter of whom has made only one appearance this season.

A laundry list of new injuries is not what the Rams needed as they find themselves at the bottom of the NFC West on Monday following a stunning loss to Arizona.

Behind the 2-4 Cardinals due to tiebreakers and staring up at the 3-3 Seahawks and unbeaten 49ers, the Rams have a long way to go to threaten for a division title -- and fewer pieces to help make it happen.

"We've taken some shots this year, and we've got to be able to get up and keep swinging," McVay said. "This is a good test."

text:
Tank Dell is back.

The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024.

"I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel.

"He is as quick as ever."

Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome.

He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day.

Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments, sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since.

The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally.

Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston.

Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here.

text:
Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, according to multiple reports, after blood clots were found in his lungs.

The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issued a joint statement on Monday laying out his updated diagnosis after originally announcing he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf that caused him to miss Week 6. A follow-up scan over the weekend revealed deep vein thrombosis, and he had "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning several blood clots were now in his lungs.

The Eagles said Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery. However, he will be treated with blood thinners, which will take him away from football activities until he is off the treatment.

Here is the full statement:

"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

It was initially diagnosed as a superficial blood clot. At that time, doctors advised Hurts not to sleep as a precaution, so he stayed awake for roughly 36 hours prior to the game against the Jaguars, according to reports. Despite not getting any sleep, Hurts started and threw for 220 yards and a touchdown.

Lynn has since clarified that Hurts was able to sleep despite being evaluated at the hospital until the early hours of Sunday morning. She said that the Eagles set up a room for him at the stadium.

No clots were found until Hurts was in London. It was later discovered that the blood clot was "provoked," meaning that it was caused by Hurts getting cleated in his calf during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. That game took place a week before Philadelphia's game in London.

Hurts traveled to London that week, appearing on that week's injury report with a calf injury on Friday. He was a full practice participant that day and had no injury designation prior to the Eagles' game against the Jaguars. Hurts reportedly went to the hospital the evening prior to Sunday's game.

Philadelphia will move forward with Tanner McKee at quarterback. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee made his first start of the season Sunday against the Panthers. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-15 loss that dropped the Eagles to 2-4.

Hurts, 28, is in his seventh season with the Eagles, who selected him in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. During his first six seasons, Hurts earned three Pro Bowl selections and helped lead the Eagles to two NFC titles and a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. He holds the single-game Super Bowl record for rushing yards by a quarterback (72 against the Chiefs). Hurts is one of just two players (the other being Terrell Davis) to run for three touchdowns in a Super Bowl game.

Hurts was named MVP of Super Bowl LIX after amassing 293 total yards and scoring three total touchdowns in the Eagles' 40-22 win over the Chiefs. Hurts has the highest career completion percentage (73.3%) in Super Bowl history among passers with at least 40 attempts.
